Heading: 'Musterrechnung. Zug von Wurzeln der Gleichung x^7 − 28x^4 + 280 + 200 cos φ = 0', i.e. a sample computation on the course of a root of this equation as φ varies.

(A) Tabulating the root. Write c(φ) = 280 + 200 cos φ, so 80 ≤ c ≤ 480. For c < 483.8 the polynomial x^7 − 28x^4 + c has two positive real roots, either side of x = 16^(1/3) ≈ 2.52. Gauss follows the smaller one, x(φ), at steps of 7.5° (inferred). Spot checks of the table:
- φ = 0, c = 480: x = 2.4580892.
- φ = 90°, c = 280: x = 1.9102070.
- φ = 180°, c = 80: x = 1.3288832.
The first line runs x(0°), x(7.5°), … down to x(90°): 13 values. The second line runs x(180°), x(172.5°), … down to x(97.5°): 12 values.

(B) Folding for a trigonometric (cosine) analysis with 48 points per period. x(φ) is even and 2π-periodic.
- First folding: s_k = x(7.5k°) + x(180° − 7.5k°) for k = 0…11, and s_12 = 2x(90°). For example s_0 = 3.7869724 and s_12 = 3.8204140.
- Second folding, sums: s_0 + s_12 = 7.6073864, s_1 + s_11 = 7.6005955, s_2 + s_10 = 7.5881721, s_3 + s_9 = 7.5779976, 2s_6 = 7.5673996, s_5 + s_7 = 7.5683701, s_4 + s_8 = 7.5716204.
- Second folding, differences: s_0 − s_12 = −0.0334416, s_2 − s_10 = −0.0427299, s_4 − s_8 = −0.0319728, α = s_1 − s_11 = −0.0377129, β = s_3 − s_9 = −0.0410596, γ = s_5 − s_7 = −0.0173973.
- Third folding: 15.1747860, 15.1689656, 15.1597925, 15.1559952, then 30.3307812 and 30.3287581.
- Total: 90.9882974 = 30.3307812 + 2·30.3287581 = x(0) + x(180°) + 2Σ_{k=1}^{23} x(7.5k°). This is the full 48-point sum, so (my step) a_0 = 90.9882974/48 ≈ 1.8955895, the mean value of the root over a period.
- The difference 30.3307812 − 30.3287581 = 0.0020231 enters the highest-order (aliasing) coefficient.

(C) Higher cosine coefficients from the difference sequences. Gauss multiplies by weights of the form (2/N)·cos(jπ/12), N = 48, done with 7-place logarithms:
- log(8√3) = 1.1416506, log(8√6) = 1.2921656, log(12√2) = 1.2296962, log(24√2) = 1.5307262, log 12 = 1.0791812, log 24 = 1.3802112.
Verified partial terms:
- 565385/24 = 23557.71.
- 322254/(8√3) = 23256.68.
- −654144/24 = −27256.00.
- −427299/(8√3) = −30837.65.
- (α+γ)/(8√6) = −28123.22.
- (α+2β−γ)/(24√2) = −30180.15.
- 305040/24 = 12710.00.
- (α−β−γ)/(12√2) = 12223.52.
Combined: −27256.00 − 30837.65 = −58093.65 and −28123.22 − 30180.15 = −58303.37. These are paired partial results (sum and difference give coefficients of order k and its complement; units 1e−7). The pairs +12710.00/+12223.52 and +3581.65/+2056.93 are of the same kind.

(D) Right-hand block. Angles in sexagesimal with fractional seconds. The pairs sum almost exactly to 22.5° or 67.5°:
- 21°52'18" + 0°37'41" ≈ 22°30'
- 21°7'48" + 1°22'41" ≈ 22°30'
- 66°49'27" + 0°40'32" ≈ 67°30'
This suggests amplitude and phase determinations by logarithms (arctan of ratios of trigonometric sums). The columns of logs (…9.99997 near 0, log 12, log 24) and the results 1318819.70/1306235.24 and 14425.16/15404.72 are the corresponding moduli.

(E) Lower block. A second analogous scheme with differences labelled α, δ, ε, β, γ, ζ and their combinations α+δ, γ−ζ, α−δ−ε, β−γ−ζ, α−δ+2ε, 2β+γ+ζ (8-digit quantities), again multiplied by the same log-weights. It ends in two rows of coefficient series, +2622245.82 + 152503.86 + 30207.30 + 10221.86 + 4769.80 + 3066.34 versus +2622054.94 + …, and 1312656.08 + 78636.83 + 20214.58 versus 1309589.74 + … . These are paired determinations of the rapidly decreasing Fourier coefficients. The next page continues the same scheme on other data.

Interpretation (partly mine): a worked example of numerical harmonic analysis of an implicitly defined periodic function, using Gauss's sum/difference reduction. This is the kind of computation described in his 'Theoria interpolationis methodo nova tractata'.
errors: No arithmetic slips found in the checked steps. Root values, foldings, the 48-point sum, the log-weights and the partial products all agree to the last digit, given the transcription corrections below.
Sub-columns 68834, 187908, 91731, 4448, +3581.65, +2056.93 and most of the lower block could not be fully traced; correctness is unverified rather than refuted.
The 7.5° step is inferred from the count of 13 + 12 values and is consistent with spot checks, but not every intermediate root was recomputed.

results.what: Tabulation of the smaller positive real root of x^7 − 28x^4 + 280 + 200 cos φ = 0 at 7.5° steps, by numerical root solving
results.modern_name: numerical root continuation / tabulation of an implicit function

results.what: Sum/difference folding of 48 equally spaced samples of an even periodic function to obtain the mean value and cosine coefficients, with weights (2/N)cos(jπ/12) applied via logarithms
results.modern_name: discrete cosine/Fourier analysis with symmetry folding (precursor of FFT-type index splitting)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Theoria interpolationis, c.1805, publ. 1866); Runge (1903) and Cooley–Tukey (1965) for later schemes

results.what: Amplitude/phase determination of harmonic terms by logarithms (angles ≈ 22.5°, 67.5° split into nearby parts)
results.modern_name: harmonic analysis: conversion of a cos + b sin to amplitude–phase form

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful worked example of Gauss's known trigonometric-interpolation and folding technique, applied to a test function defined as a root of a polynomial depending on cos φ. The method is already credited to Gauss (Werke III; Heideman–Johnson–Burrus 1984). The specific test example is a minor unpublished detail.
